title: Fix drop shadow filter SWF export: 99% visual oracle mismatch
description:
The new visual-oracle E2E fixture 'drop shadow filter renders consistently' (apps/desktop/e2e/visual-oracle.spec.ts) fails with 99.2% pixel mismatch — near-total rendering failure.

The fixture creates a white rectangle with a drop shadow (blur=4, distance=4, angle=45) and compares the authoring CanvasRenderer output against Ruffle's SWF playback. A 99% mismatch means one side is essentially blank.

Likely causes to investigate:
1. The drop shadow filter is not being encoded into the SWF at all — check packages/swf/src/filters.ts encodeDropShadowFilter() and verify the FILTERLIST record is attached to the PlaceObject3 tag for the shape.
2. The SWF is using PlaceObject2 (tag 26) instead of PlaceObject3 (tag 70) — filters require PlaceObject3. Check packages/swf/src/compile.ts: when a display object has filters, the encoder must emit PlaceObject3 not PlaceObject2.
3. The filter record byte encoding is malformed — fuzz the filter ID byte (0x00 for DropShadow) and parameter count.
4. The CanvasRenderer is applying the drop shadow via CSS filter but the SWF encodes it differently (different blur radius units: SWF uses 20ths-of-a-pixel for blur, CSS uses px directly).

Debug steps:
- Save both screenshots via testInfo.attach() when the test fails (already wired in the spec).
- Run: pnpm --filter @flash/desktop e2e -- e2e/visual-oracle.spec.ts --grep 'drop shadow'
- Inspect the attached PNGs to determine which side is blank.
- Parse the SWF bytes: check that a PlaceObject3 tag with FILTERLIST appears.

Acceptance: the drop shadow fixture passes at <= 20% mismatch.
